steps: Reviewed earlier first-three shape lemma supplies the mode inequalities; the ordered-conductance theorem supplies negative nonzero cooling overlaps.

Conditional mean on first three states is a constant plus nonnegative multiples of averages of (1,-1,0) and (1,1,-2). Both derivatives are positive for ordered energies at beta>=0, so the conditional mean is nondecreasing.
First-three mass P strictly increases and obeys 3/4<P<1 at finite beta>0. Thus r=P_c/P_h is greater than one and strictly below 4/3.
The identity b_c-r b_h=P_c(m_c-m_h)+(1-r)w4 has two nonnegative terms. Since both overlaps are negative, the absolute ratio is at most r<4/3. Equality is impossible at finite admissible parameters.

Both sharpness constructions approach ratio 4/3 for actual admissible finite preparations. Hence the bound is the sharp supremum. The KL leading quadratic coefficient gives advantage 1-(3/4)^2=7/16. The asymptotic threshold-time shift is log(|b_c|/|b_h|)/|lambda2|<log(4/3)/|lambda2|; this is not a finite-threshold universal time-saving statement.

Transcribed all three denominator polynomials and six rate formulas from SharpFamily.lean and matched the formal sharpness appendix term by term. The correspondence checker independently verifies exact eigen-equations, detailed balance, conservation, and all six rate limits.
Bath weights are strictly decreasing and positive for 0<epsilon<1/30. The mode has first component one and exact zero bath mean. Denominators P,-R,S have positive values at zero.

All thirteen continuity functions are rational with nonzero denominators at zero; their values are 68,12,21,3/2,20/17,15/7,20/17,12/17,9/14,117/70,66/425,276/595,1/17. A finite intersection of neighborhoods supplies simultaneous strict positivity for sufficiently small positive epsilon.

F124 and G234 vanish identically. The factorization e_rate-c_rate*t=epsilon*positive_function gives strict G124; G234 equality then gives strict G134. The remaining three F and G123 signs are among the thirteen checks. Positive clearing factors preserve original F signs.
Reconstructed all three positive contrast coordinates: the first uses w1-w2>0, the last uses w4<0, and the middle is the sum of positive multiples of -w3 and -w4. w3<0 for 0<epsilon<1/30.
Two strict G margins give strictly positive contrast edges connecting coordinate one to coordinates two and three. Other off-diagonals are nonnegative.

PositiveMode.lean proves the weighted-defect quadratic identity as a sum of nonnegative squared ratios. It proves maximal eigenvalue ordering and shows the kernel is one-dimensional from the two connecting edges. No assumed uniform gap or numerical eigenvalue is substituted.
The bridge reconstructs the full mode and transfers the positive-coordinate eigen-equation, variational ordering and one-dimensional eigenspace to SimpleSlowMode of the full generator.

The listed endpoint values and optional critical value are therefore the exact infimum/supremum on each bath side. Opposite strict signs occur in the open interval if and only if the finite list has min<0<max; limiting strict signs persist at finite beta by continuity.

Strict convexity gives at most two derivative zeros counting multiplicity: a nonvertical line meets a strictly convex graph at most twice, tangency has exactly order two, and C=0 has at most one. Identically zero derivative would force constant w by independence of exponentials, excluded by nonzero bath-orthogonal w.

If bprime has one sign on a bath side, bath value zero forces normal magnitude order. For opposite signs on cooling, the last sign-changing zero before the bath has nonzero b and creates increasing magnitude immediately to its left. For heating use the first sign-changing zero after the bath and decreasing magnitude immediately to its right.
Tangencies without opposite signs do not suffice. A stationary bath or an endpoint equality does not create an additional interior root. Finite positive witnesses follow from the open sign intervals.

steps: The bath-mean-zero subspace perpendicular to w in the D inner product has dimension two. Rational Gaussian elimination produces U when inputs are rational.
Signed core M0=-D U B U^T has zero column sums, detailed balance, and null left vectors 1,w. Its symmetric form is -(D^1/2 U) B (D^1/2 U)^T.

Adding rho(q 1^T-I) shifts every nonstationary rate by -rho and permits strictly positive off-diagonal rates for sufficiently large rho. It leaves all F,G unchanged.
Conversely M+lambda2(q 1^T-I) removes the simple slow eigenvalue and is strictly negative on its two-dimensional complement. A full-rank basis U therefore gives a positive definite B by congruence.
Trace scaling preserves homogeneous F,G constraints. For B=[[1+x,y],[y,1-x]]/2, eigenvalues are (1 +/- sqrt(x^2+y^2))/2, so positive definiteness requires the open unit disk, not its boundary.

The minimum-norm point of any nonempty closed half-plane intersection is the origin, a projection to one active boundary line, or an intersection of two independent active lines. This also covers lines, rays, points, and unbounded polyhedra.
The exact constructor enumerates all those rational candidates, rejects infeasible candidates and radius >=1, and treats inconsistent constant constraints separately.
Its reported gap det(B)det(U^T D U)/trace(B U^T D U) equals nu1 nu2/(nu1+nu2), a positive lower bound smaller than each fast gap. Rho=max(core_ij,0)+gap/100 guarantees strict rates.
Positive slack strengthens the half-planes, so infeasibility there cannot exclude the original problem. The return data and regression checks preserve this scope.
The existing first-contrast regression attains exact minimum squared radius one and is correctly rejected. Independent rational LDL inertia brackets the accepted slow eigenvalue.

steps: Under the contrast orientation b is strictly negative throughout cooling, including beta=0, and each prefix overlap has a strictly positive derivative at the bath, so bprime(beta_b)>0.
For C=w3-w4>=0, the first-three arithmetic restriction makes the conditional mean at zero at least w3>=w4. Its monotonicity gives bprime=P mprime+Pprime(m-w4)>0.
Strictness holds because either the first-three contrast decomposition is nonconstant and mprime>0, or those three entries coincide and bath mean zero with a nonconstant full mode gives m>w4.
For C<0, the derivative-curve representation Phi=A+B u+C v(u) is strictly concave, since v is strictly convex. Its left endpoint is w1-w2>=0 and its bath value is positive.

If the zero-temperature-parameter endpoint Phi(u(0)) is nonnegative, strict concavity places every interior value above the nonnegative endpoint chord, so derivative is strictly positive for every finite beta>0, including endpoint equality.

If Phi(u(0))<0, concavity and the positive bath value give exactly one right-hand crossing, with no additional left-hand interior zero. Since u decreases with beta, derivative is negative before the turn and positive afterward.

The turn lies strictly between zero and bath. Because b<0 on cooling, absolute magnitude has its unique maximum there; negative endpoint derivative persists at small finite positive beta and gives admissible witnesses.
Covariance identity at uniform beta=0 gives the stated sign test. It concerns existence of an asymptotic anomaly and does not decide all transient crossings.
